issues.body: Every new `#[cfg(not(feature = "engine"))]` branch returns an exact vocabulary-IRI comparison, but the corresponding rows remain `Coverage::Pass` and contribute to `REQUIREMENTS_FLOOR`. In that feature state there is no evaluator, so these checks cannot establish any of R1/R2/R3/R7/R8/R14/R18's graph-pattern behavior. This is the same class of non-conformance-sensitive probe that the new comment correctly criticizes; changing `ends_with` to exact equality only validates constants, not the stated requirements.
issues.fix_hint: Do not count these requirements as passing when `engine` is disabled. Gate the graph-pattern requirement rows/test on `engine`, or represent them as gaps/not-applicable outside that feature while ensuring the committed conformance floor is derived from the feature-enabled run. Add a feature-off test that verifies the rows cannot be reported as demonstrated merely from vocabulary constants.
issues.title: Feature-off checks still count vacuous graph-pattern coverage as passing

issues.body: The R1 statement remains `Support SPARQL Query + Protocol + the geo: ontology vocabulary`, yet `core_sparql_query_over_geo_vocab` calls only `sparq_engine::query`. The new module prose says HTTP transport is requirement-agnostic and explicitly removes the prior server-test evidence, leaving the Protocol portion of the recorded passing requirement untested. An in-process evaluator is not a SPARQL Protocol endpoint.
issues.fix_hint: Either retain/add a real protocol-level probe using a GeoSPARQL-vocabulary fixture, or narrow/split the requirement and coverage accounting so this row does not claim Protocol conformance based solely on `sparq_engine::query`.
issues.title: R1 claims Query + Protocol but tests only in-process query evaluation

verdict.summary: The default-feature probes materially improve the test by exercising real graph-pattern evaluation, but the change is not complete across the supported feature states. With `--no-default-features`, all seven requirements remain recorded as `Coverage::Pass` while their checks only compare vocabulary strings and cannot detect the absence or failure of SPARQL graph-pattern support. This directly preserves the vacuity the PR says it removes. R1 also still states Query + Protocol support while its replacement probe exercises only in-process query evaluation and the new prose dismisses protocol coverage without changing the claimed requirement.
